directive: When hits include T-cell receptor signaling or early TCR activation components, prioritize untested genes in adaptor proteins, protein tyrosine kinases, and NF-κB pathway members, as TCR-proximal signaling cascades show consistent enrichment across immune phenotypes.

When hits include vesicular trafficking or endosomal sorting components, prioritize untested genes in the ubiquitin-proteasome system and RNA-binding protein families, as these three pathways co-enrich in cellular homeostasis and protein quality control phenotypes.

When hits include autophagy machinery or lysosomal transport components, prioritize untested genes in lipid metabolism, cholesterol trafficking, and ER-lysosome membrane contact pathways, as these coordinate in lysosomal homeostasis and recycling phenotypes.

When hits include adenosine signaling or GPCR pathway components, prioritize untested genes in purine/nucleotide metabolism and cAMP/PKA signaling scaffolds, as these pathways coordinate immunosuppressive signal transduction.

When hits include Mediator complex or general transcription factor (TFIID/TAF) components, prioritize untested genes in histone modification, chromatin remodeling, and transcriptional co-activator families, as these form an integrated transcriptional regulatory module.

When hits include proteasome subunits or core proteasomal degradation machinery, prioritize untested genes in ubiquitin conjugation, E2/E3 ligase families, and deubiquitinase complexes, as protein degradation is a coordinated multi-step process.

When hits include IL-2 receptor signaling or STAT pathway components, prioritize untested genes in T-cell transcriptional regulators and immune checkpoint modulators, as these coordinate T-cell activation and differentiation states.

When overall hit rate falls in the 4–5% range (moderate signal density), employ online adaptive machine learning strategies to iteratively refine gene prioritization, as this regime shows consistent ML advantage over single-pass reasoning.

When overall hit rate is very low (<3%), employ LLM-based reasoning strategies that leverage domain knowledge and pathway semantics, as sparse signal favors interpretable hypothesis-driven selection over statistical learning.

When screening a small, curated gene set (≤1000 genes) with high hit density (≥9%), use LLM reasoning to maximize signal extraction from limited search space, as domain knowledge becomes more valuable when the candidate pool is pre-filtered.

When screening large gene sets (>9000 genes), weight online adaptive ML strategies more heavily than single-pass LLM reasoning in early rounds, as statistical learning scales better with search space size and hit density.

When hits span multiple functional modules (e.g., signaling + transcription + chromatin), prioritize untested genes that bridge or coordinate between those modules, as phenotypes often require multi-layer regulatory integration rather than single-pathway dominance.
